1. The animation shows how a 7.40% mortgage rate compares with history. It uses the Freddie Mac weekly mortgage survey, covering Aug 1991 to Oct 2026. A dashed line marks 7.40%. The weeks at or above that line are highlighted in orange-yellow, mostly in the early 1990s. The caption says only about 1 week in 5 had a rate this high. The scene includes a character named Tessa, a house, and a small money icon at the right end of the line. The labels say "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "US only · history, not a forecast."

2. Frame 1 has only the chart. Frame 2 adds the caption and a row of five blue squares. From frame 3 on, one square turns orange to show the 1-in-5 share. The chart itself doesn't move between frames. The line ends near the 7.40% level at Oct 2026, after a long dip and a recent sharp rise.

3. It means that a rate of 7.40% is high compared with the last 35 years. Most weeks had lower rates, and only about 20% had rates this high or higher. The "history, not a forecast" label says this is a look back and doesn't predict where rates will go.

4. The animation gives no direct advice. A viewer might infer that today's rate is historically high, and might then think about refinancing later if rates fall. The animation doesn't say that, and it says nothing about paying extra on a mortgage versus investing.

5. The inference in 4 is my own conclusion. The animation only gave the historical comparison and the "not a forecast" disclaimer. It did not recommend anything.
